meta.title: Operation Glass House: NCII Double Extortion
meta.summary: A sophisticated threat actor has breached a National Critical Information Infrastructure (NCII) hub. The crisis evolves from a standard ransomware lockout to a personal, high-stakes psychological war targeting the Board directly.

questions.text: Early monitoring detects anomalous encryption on back-office servers. Technical teams request a partial 'protective' shutdown of external gateways. What is your directive?
questions.context: A shutdown protects the core but immediately halts public revenue collection.

answers.label: Prioritize Containment: Authorize shutdown
answers.description: Accept disruption to prevent lateral movement into critical control systems.
answers.boardReading: Safety-first. Minimizes technical risk but creates public visibility.
answers.consequence: Lateral movement is slowed, but media begins reporting an 'outage' within minutes.

answers.label: Prioritize Continuity: Maintain services
answers.description: Isolate affected servers without a full block to avoid public panic.
answers.boardReading: Aggressive continuity focus. Risks wider breach for appearance's sake.
answers.consequence: Service stays up, but the attacker exfiltrates 500GB of sensitive data.

questions.text: The attacker confirms exfiltration of Board minutes and customer records. They demand $10M. How do you respond?
questions.context: This is now a liability and reputational crisis.

answers.label: Engage Law Enforcement and refuse negotiation
answers.description: Maintain 'No Pay' policy, accelerate data breach notifications.
answers.boardReading: Principled and legally defensive. Expects high reputational damage.
answers.consequence: The attacker begins leaking 'proof samples' to dark web forums.

answers.label: Appoint a negotiator to stall
answers.description: Open a dialogue to buy technical recovery time, without promising payment.
answers.boardReading: Tactical. Buys the team 24 hours but risks escalating attacker aggression.
answers.consequence: The attacker grows impatient and realizes they are being stalled.

questions.text: WILDCARD: Board members receive photos of their children and home addresses. Attacker threatens 'physical consequences' if not paid in 4 hours.
questions.context: The crisis is now in the home. Personal safety is at stake.

answers.label: Authorize emergency protective security
answers.description: Engage security/police to protect families while maintaining corporate refusal to pay.
answers.boardReading: Separates personal safety from policy. High cost but preserves integrity.
answers.consequence: Board remains united but under strain; attacker prepares a 'media bomb'.

answers.label: Discuss 'Continuity Payment'
answers.description: Consider paying solely to end the personal threat to families.
answers.boardReading: Safety-first but sets a dangerous precedent for physical extortion.
answers.consequence: Payment is made, but attacker leaks the data anyway.

questions.text: WILDCARD: Press receives leaked minutes and info on the personal threats. They demand a 'come clean' statement.
questions.context: Silence is no longer an option.

answers.label: Full Transparency: Live press conference
answers.description: Acknowledge breach, theft, and appalling threats. State refusal to be coerced.
answers.boardReading: Radical transparency. Seizes narrative and garner sympathy.
answers.consequence: Reputational hit is massive, but public trust begins to stabilize.

answers.label: Controlled Response: Written legal statement
answers.description: Confirm 'incident' investigation; warn press about publishing stolen data.
answers.boardReading: Legalistic. Likely seen as a cover-up by public and press.
answers.consequence: Press publishes leaked minutes regardless; org looks deceptive.
